_comment: Instances that MUST FAIL validation, expressed as single mutations of real examples. Run by tools/validate_counterexamples.py; see that file's docstring and docs/SILENT_SUCCESS.md section 1. Each case asserts that one constraint still BITES: the mutation is applied in memory, the result must be rejected, and it must be rejected for the reason named in `expect`. A case that starts passing means the constraint stopped applying, which no positive example can detect.

_fields.example: repo-relative path to a VALID example; the schema is its sibling resolvedSchema.json
_fields.mutate: one of {op: remove|set|add, pointer: <JSON Pointer>, value: <for set/add>}
_fields.expect: substring that must appear in the rejection's message, schema path or instance path
_fields.why: what constraint this defends and why losing it would be invisible

cases.why: Without @context the document has no term mapping, so every ada:/schema: key is uninterpretable as JSON-LD while remaining perfectly well-formed JSON. Nothing downstream would notice until a consumer tried to expand it.

schema:name is what separates an INLINE TAPP plan from a bare {@id, @type} REFERENCE to one. geochemProduct's TAPP conditional guards its `if` on schema:name for exactly that reason -- keyed on @type alone it held every reference and failed it on the four properties a reference does not carry. If name stops being required, inline plans and references become indistinguishable and that conditional silently stops separating them.
The technique is the one thing a TAPP must declare; a protocol that does not say what technique it is cannot be matched to a profile.

A TAPP carries several required @type members (ada:TAPPDefinition and prov:Plan among them -- the plan typing is a deliberate PROV decision, not decoration). Accepting an arbitrary single @type would let a document claim to be a TAPP without being one, and the conditionals that key on @type would stop firing.

schema:variableMeasured stopped being required OUTRIGHT on 2026-10-16, when cdifDataDescription became conditional in geochemProduct: 7,439 of 7,447 ADA records carry no variables because they are images, documents or collections with nothing to describe, and requiring it of them made almost no record declarable. This case was written against the old unconditional rule and had to be REPLACED rather than deleted -- the requirement did not vanish, it became conditional, and the conditional needs a floor. The floor is the tabular limb: a record carrying TABULAR data has columns to describe, so removing its variables must still be rejected. The example is MONOLITHIC, which is the half that is easy to lose: it carries cdi:TabularTextDataSet on the distribution ITSELF with no schema:hasPart, so a hasPart-only condition misses it entirely. The first draft of the conditional was hasPart-only and this case caught it -- the collection-only trap CLAUDE.md's three-levels rule names.

Each file-type BB declares a SEALED enum of componentType strings, derived from the Components worksheet, so that e.g. ada:EPMAImageMap only validates on a part typed ada:imageMap. The enum is the whole mechanism; an unsealed one would let any componentType sit on any part, and check_componentType.py cannot see that because the base layer is annotation-only.

files/schema.yaml's outer anyOf deliberately has NO permissive schema:MediaObject fallback, so a part whose @type matches no specific file-type BB must fail. That absence is a design decision recorded in CLAUDE.md, and adding a fallback 'to be helpful' would make every unrecognised part validate silently.

@id is REQUIRED on an instrument (and on an inline schema:hasPart component) because a monitored species has to be able to name the device that reports it. Generated ids are ex:instrument/<Token>, stable across regenerations. Without the requirement the reference target simply does not exist and nothing points anywhere.

An untyped variable entry cannot be dispatched to the right shape, and @type is what every conditional in the product schema keys on. A missing @type matches no `if`, so the constraints that should apply are silently absent and the record validates clean -- the too-narrow-conditional failure mode in CLAUDE.md.

A generated technique requirement, from the EPMA table's tier columns. This is the class of constraint that went missing unnoticed in 2026-09-03, when nine ICP-MS schemas lost 'Limit of Quantification (LOQ) Method' and validate_examples stayed green: a requiredness that evaporates makes the schema more permissive, so every example still passes.

A keyed-table COLUMN is always a schema:PropertyValueSpecification on the procedure side: a column DEFINITION specifies, a property on a part RECORDS. Read-only is an attribute of the specification (schema:readonlyValue), not a different type. Emitting PropertyValue here once produced an allOf no instance could satisfy; the inverse -- accepting PropertyValue -- would let the two shapes merge and the distinction stop meaning anything.

ada:dataType carries the column's declared type and is where unit extraction comes from. A column with no declared type is unusable by a form builder or a loader, and the mismatch between declared and emitted shape is exactly what hid the ada:collectorConfiguration defect until 2026-09-27.

A workflow-step parameter with no name cannot be joined back to the TAPP table row it came from. It also guards the step subtree itself: a standalone build_pathdriven run once dropped the whole schema:actionProcess subtree -- 74 JSON paths -- at a green 614/26, so a case anchored inside a step is a tripwire for that subtree going missing.

A method's standard workflow must include exactly one sample-preparation step. The rule lives on $defs/MethodWorkflowHowTo, which only the TOP-LEVEL schema:actionProcess references -- it used to sit on WorkflowHowTo, which is ALSO a step's sub-workflow, so a sample-preparation step broken into mount/grind/polish/coat would have needed a nested "Sample preparation" inside itself. Splitting the two $defs removed the requirement from 59 detail blocks (177 constraints), so this case is what proves the half that should have survived did.

A workflow step must carry all THREE @type members. cdi:Activity and schema:Action give the DDI-CDI and schema.org process semantics; schema:HowToStep is what schema.org expects of a schema:step value on a schema:HowTo, and the base cdifProvActivity requires it too. The two sides disagreed for a long time without anything failing -- 565 steps carried the first two and 15 carried HowToStep alone, depending on which emitter wrote them. This case fails the moment the third member stops being required.

The sample-preparation discriminator was widened to accept either serialization of bios:LabProcess -- the bare CURIE or a JSON-LD IRI reference -- because CDIF's SHACL asks for the latter and the JSON Schema previously forbade it. A widened `contains` is exactly the 'if too broad' hazard: written loosely it would match ANY step object and silently satisfy the requirement, failing nothing. This pins the new branch by giving it the right SHAPE and the wrong VALUE: {"@id": "bios:NotLabProcess"} must still be rejected on `contains`. Its sibling case method-workflow-requires-sample-prep pins that removing the step entirely is rejected; this pins that the @id branch discriminates rather than merely accepting objects.

An analysed sample must be IDENTIFIABLE. `schema:name` used to be required outright, which rejected every ADA record of all 8 legacy cids that have a TAPP replacement -- the records name the sample with `schema:identifier` ("OREX-803031-101") and carry no separate laboratory name -- so schema_path_emitter.SUBSTITUTES now lets the identifier satisfy the name, scoped to `schema:object`. What must NOT follow is that a sample can be anonymous. This case sets the sample to a bare typed object carrying NEITHER, and it must still be rejected. It is a `set` rather than a `remove` because no example carries a name without an identifier, so removing one leaves the other and tests nothing. Its partners are `tappdef-requires-name` and `step-parameter-requires-name`, which hold the other side of the line: at those nodes an identifier is NOT an acceptable substitute, and a global relaxation would have silently voided both.

adaProduct's own layer had NO required list at all until 2026-10-16, so a record could declare ADA conformance and be tested on almost nothing ADA-specific. This is the first of the three requirements that fixed that, and it is the one with a sequencing hazard worth remembering: ADA had to EMIT ada:submissionType across all 7,447 records BEFORE gBB could require it, because requiring it first would have failed the entire corpus rather than 16 records. The property is also PREFIXED -- it was a bare `submissionType`, which in JSON-LD does not expand to an IRI without an @context term, so it was a dangling key. The rename had to travel with the requirement, and this case pins the prefixed spelling.

schema:additionalType has carried the 127-label product-type `contains` for as long as it has existed, and that constraint did NOTHING for a record that simply omitted the property -- an absent property is never checked. Requiring it, on 2026-10-16, makes the existing enum mandatory rather than conditional on the author having volunteered the field. The mutation REMOVES the property rather than replacing its value, and that distinction is the whole case: a replaced value is caught by the pre-existing `contains` and was already rejected before this requirement existed, so such a case would pass while testing the older constraint and tell you nothing about the new one. Verified both ways against origin/main's schema -- removal was accepted there and is rejected here.

A delivery has to say what KIND of files it carries, which is the claim adaProduct exists to make. Either shape satisfies it -- a monolithic distribution carrying ada:componentType itself, or a bundle carrying one on a schema:hasPart member -- because requiring only the hasPart form would foreclose the monolithic case the schema deliberately supports. This mutation empties hasPart while leaving the key present, which is precisely the shape of the 41 corpus records this requirement newly fails: a collection declaring no parts, distinct from a monolithic distribution and distinct again from an absent key (0 records). `expect` cannot name ada:componentType: a failing `contains` reports the whole array and its schema path stops at `contains`, the same message problem recorded for anyOf in CLAUDE.md. The instance path is what identifies the constraint here.
